title: Human Embryonic Development: Germ Layers & Organs Guide
description: Explore human embryonic development from weeks three to eight, covering gastrulation, three germ layers, neural tube closure, somite pairs, and organ plan.
h1: Human Embryonic Development: Germ Layers, Neural Tube and Organs
blurb: Weeks three to eight: gastrulation establishes ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm as the neural tube closes, somites segment, and major organ systems take shape.
lead: Between the third and eighth weeks after conception, a flat three-layered embryonic disc folds into a recognizable body plan with a beating heart and neural tube. In this illustrated guide to human embryonic development, we examine 20 documented structures—including embryonic disc, primitive streak, gastrulation, ectoderm—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Between the third and eighth weeks after conception, a flat three-layered embryonic disc folds into a recognizable body plan with a beating heart and neural tube. After implantation, the embryonic disc establishes ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm during gastrulation. Neurulation and body folding organize an early body plan, while early heart, gut, somites and limb buds form. In standard embryology the embryonic period of major organ formation covers approximately weeks 3–8 after fertilization, roughly two weeks less than corresponding obstetric gestational age; exact morphology varies. From the following developmental period, the term fetus emphasizes growth and maturation. The image is a stylized single early-developing human and is NOT a week-accurate clinical scan, histology image, or a reliable depiction of any specific day; no unidentifiable microscopic parts receive pins. questions.question: What are the three embryonic germ layers?
questions.answer: Gastrulation establishes ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. Together they contribute to later organs and tissues, though any one organ often draws from more than one layer.

questions.question: What does the embryonic neural tube form?
questions.answer: The embryonic neural tube develops into the brain and spinal cord after the neural plate folds and closes.

questions.question: When does major embryonic organ formation occur?
questions.answer: A standard developmental convention describes much organ-plan formation during roughly weeks three through eight after fertilization. Obstetric gestational weeks counted from the LMP are usually about two weeks higher.

questions.question: How does a flat embryonic disc become a body shape?
questions.answer: Head, tail and lateral folds transform the disc into a three-dimensional body and help position the primitive gut. The still digital plate shows a simplified later form, not actual folding in motion.

questions.question: Is the illustrated early human an exact image of week eight?
questions.answer: No. It is a stylized non-diagnostic model rather than a measured clinical image or week-specific specimen. Form and timing vary, so age cannot be determined from the rendering.
